newsitem.title: UK: British government to soldier on - Mawhinney.
newsitem.headline: British government to soldier on - Mawhinney.

text.p: The British government will carry on in office so long as it can win votes in Parliament, the chairman of the Conservative Party said on Friday.

Brian Mawhinney was speaking after a by-election, which robbed the party of its overall parliamentary majority for the first time since 1979. "As long as we have majorities (in Parliament) that are deliverable on a regular basis, we will continue to govern," he said.

A widely expected victory for the opposition Labour Party in the by-election in the northern England seat of Barnsley East means that the 323 Conservative members of parliament are now matched by the same number of opposition legislators.
Labour's Jeff Ennis won a majority of 12,181 votes over the minority Liberal Democrat candidate, with the Conservative challenger sinking to a lowly third place.
"The government is going to find it increasingly a problem getting its business (through Parliament)," Donald Dewar, parliamentary business manager for Labour told BBC radio.

The government's position had already been weakened last week when one of its legislators, Sir John Gorst, said he was withdrawing support from Prime Minister John Major because of a row over hospital facilities in his North London constituency.
